title: Same Salary… So Why Does Your Little Sister Repay Almost £400 More? 😱🎓 #shorts
description:
Same salary, yet your little sister repays almost £400 more a year, because she started uni in autumn 2023.

Student loans in England taken out for courses starting on or after 1 August 2023 are Plan 5; courses that started between 1 September 2012 and 31 July 2023 are Plan 2. Both take 9% of your income above a threshold. In 2026/27 Plan 5 starts at £25,000 a year; Plan 2 waits until £29,385 (nearly £30,000). On £36,000 a year, paid monthly, that's £82 a month on Plan 5 vs £49 on Plan 2: £984 vs £588 a year, £396 more (on yearly income the gap is £394.65 for any salary above £29,385).

The part nobody tells her: whatever's left at the end is cancelled. Plan 2 is cancelled 30 years after you're due to start repaying; Plan 5 runs for 40, ten years longer. Her interest is a bit lower: Plan 5 is RPI (4.1% from 1 September 2026), while Plan 2 on £36,000 is about 4.9% (RPI rising to RPI + 3% between £29,385 and £52,885, capped at 6% until 31 August 2027).

Sources: https://www.gov.uk/repaying-your-student-loan/what-you-pay · https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/payroll-technical-specifications-student-loans/collection-of-student-loans-from-6-april-2026 · https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/student-loans-a-guide-to-terms-and-conditions/student-loans-a-guide-to-terms-and-conditions-2026-to-2027 · https://www.gov.uk/government/news/student-loans-interest-rates-and-repayment-threshold-announcement--7 · https://www.gov.uk/guidance/how-interest-is-calculated-plan-2
